newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money eases after repo cash injection.
newsitem.headline: German call money eases after repo cash injection.

text.p: German call money rates eased to around three percent on Wednesday from Tuesday's 3.05/10 percent as market liquidity was boosted by a 3.5 billion-mark cash injection at the Bundesbank's weekly repo allocation.
Dealers said the fresh cash gave them adequate -- but not excessive -- liquidity to cope in the run-up to the month-end reserve requirement deadline.
Commercial banks' deposits on Tuesday totalled 39.3 billion marks, up from Monday's 37.4 billion, with the daily average for the month through Tuesday unchanged at 38.3 billion.
That is well above the provisional September reserve requirement of 37.7 billion marks.
Lombard borrowings remained about 100 million marks on Tuesday. The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA was 3.05200 percent on Wednesday compared with Wednesday's 3.09500 percent.

The Bundesbank today allocated 67.8 billion marks in repos at a fixed rate of three percent. A repo pact for 64.3 billion marks at a fixed 3.00 percent expired, so a net 3.5 billion marks flowed into the market.
